scenarios.name: Place an order
scenarios.reason: Confirmation omits the required coffee and shipping breakdown, so the checkpoint cannot pass.
scenarios.diagnosis: The test added an extra confirmation-page requirement. The objective only requires confirmation that the order is in and that €17.90 was charged; it does not require the page to show separate coffee and shipping amounts.
scenarios.suggestion: Update the confirmation assertion to check that the order is confirmed and that the charged total is €17.90. Only require a separate €13.00 coffee and €4.90 shipping breakdown if that is an explicit product requirement.

scenarios.name: Free shipping from €50
scenarios.reason:
Added House Espresso and Paper Filters to the bag and opened the bag page.
The bag initially showed €4.90 shipping and a €49.40 total.
Pressed the plus button next to Paper Filters once.
The bag now shows Free shipping and a €51.00 total.

scenarios.name: Promo code total
scenarios.reason: The bag reports “That code doesn't work,” so the required discount cannot be verified without disallowed retry.
scenarios.diagnosis: The promo-code field changed the correctly entered lowercase code to uppercase, and the bag then said that the required code did not work.
scenarios.suggestion: Keep the required lowercase promo code unchanged when it is entered, or validate it without treating the changed capitalization as a different code; then confirm the cart shows −€9.10, Free shipping, and €81.90.
